subject: verbal
question: “The new drainage plan aims to mitigate the effects of flooding in low-lying barangays.” The word “mitigate” most nearly means:
explanation: To mitigate is to make something less severe, so “lessen” fits a plan meant to reduce flood damage. Predicting or recording floods would not reduce their effects.

subject: verbal
question: Which word is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to “frugal”?
explanation: A frugal person spends little, while an extravagant person spends too much. “Thrifty” is the trap: it is a synonym of frugal, not its opposite.

subject: verbal
question: “The inspector gave the documents only a perfunctory glance before signing the clearance.” The word “perfunctory” most nearly means:
explanation: Perfunctory describes something done as a routine, with little attention, so “quick and superficial” is right. The words “only” and “glance” also rule out “long and careful.”

subject: verbal
question: “The delay in relief goods only exacerbated the tension in the evacuation center.” The word “exacerbated” most nearly means:
explanation: To exacerbate is to make a bad situation worse, so “worsened” is correct. “Revealed” is tempting, but the delay increased the tension instead of merely exposing it.

subject: verbal
question: “The new ordinance abrogates the earlier rule on street vending.” The word “abrogates” most nearly means:
explanation: To abrogate a law or rule is to abolish it formally, which is what “repeals” means. “Reinforces” says nearly the opposite.

subject: verbal
question: “Dalisay ang hangarin ng guro na matulungan ang kaniyang mga mag-aaral.” Ano ang kasingkahulugan ng salitang “dalisay”?
explanation: Ang dalisay ay nangangahulugang puro o walang halong ibang layunin, kaya “wagas” ang tamang sagot. Inilalarawan nito ang hangarin ng guro, hindi ang kaniyang pag-iingat o katahimikan.

subject: verbal
question: “Masalimuot ang proseso ng pagkuha ng permiso kaya maraming aplikante ang humihingi ng tulong.” Ano ang kahulugan ng salitang “masalimuot”?
explanation: Ang masalimuot ay nangangahulugang magulo o maraming sangkot na bahagi, kaya “magulo at mahirap unawain” ang tama. Lohikal na bunga nito ang paghingi ng tulong ng mga aplikante.

subject: verbal
question: “Nagpupuyos ang kalooban ng mga magsasaka nang malaman nilang inilipat sa iba ang kanilang lupa.” Ano ang ibig sabihin ng “nagpupuyos ang kalooban”?
explanation: Ang nagpupuyos ay naglalarawan ng matinding galit na parang nag-aapoy sa loob, kaya “labis na nagagalit” ang tama. Maaaring malungkot din ang mga magsasaka, ngunit hindi lungkot ang isinasaad ng salita.

subject: verbal
question: “Ayon sa hinuha ng imbestigador, nagmula ang sunog sa lumang kable sa kusina.” Ano ang kahulugan ng salitang “hinuha”?
explanation: Ang hinuha ay palagay o konklusyong nabuo mula sa mga nakitang katibayan, kaya “palagay batay sa katibayan” ang tama. Hindi ito simpleng tala, sapagkat may pagpapasiya ang imbestigador tungkol sa pinagmulan ng sunog.

subject: verbal
question: The applicant, together with her two sisters, ____ waiting outside the examination room.
explanation: The subject is the singular “applicant”; a phrase introduced by “together with” does not change the number of the subject, so the verb is “is.”

subject: verbal
question: Because the instructions were vague, many applicants were ____ about which form to submit.
explanation: Vague instructions naturally leave people unsure, so “confused” completes the cause and effect. “Certain” says the reverse of what the first clause leads you to expect.

subject: verbal
question: The typhoon destroyed the only bridge to the island; ____, relief goods had to be delivered by boat.
explanation: Delivery by boat is the result of the bridge being destroyed, so a result word is needed: “consequently.” “Nevertheless” would signal a contrast that the two clauses do not have.

subject: verbal
question: If I ____ the head of the agency, I would simplify the application process.
explanation: The clause states an unreal present condition, shown by “would simplify” in the main clause, and that calls for the subjunctive “were.” The other forms do not pair with “would” in this kind of conditional.

subject: verbal
question: The senator's argument was so ____ that even her critics admitted it was hard to refute, for every claim rested on evidence and every objection was answered.
explanation: Cogent means clear, logical and convincing, which matches an argument its critics could not easily refute. “Verbose” only means wordy and says nothing about how strong the reasoning is.

subject: verbal
question: Nag-aral siya ____ mabuti kaya pumasa siya sa pagsusulit.
explanation: Ginagamit ang “nang” bago ang pang-abay na pamaraan, na nagsasaad kung paano ginawa ang kilos, kaya “nag-aral nang mabuti” ang wasto. Ang “ng” ay pananda ng pangngalan at hindi ng ganitong paglalarawan.

subject: verbal
question: Hindi natuloy ang pagpupulong ____ malakas ang ulan sa buong lalawigan.
explanation: Sanhi ng hindi pagkatuloy ng pagpupulong ang malakas na ulan, kaya pangatnig na nagsasaad ng dahilan ang kailangan: “sapagkat.” Ang “upang” ay para sa layunin at ang “subalit” ay para sa pagsalungat.

subject: verbal
question: Bukas pa ____ ng komisyon ang resulta ng pagsusulit.
explanation: Ang “bukas” ay tumutukoy sa panahong darating, kaya aspektong kontemplatibo ang kailangan: “ilalabas.” Tapos na ang kilos sa “inilabas” at kasalukuyang nagaganap naman sa “inilalabas.”

subject: verbal
question: ____ mo ang mga tuyong dahon bago mo diligan ang mga halaman.
explanation: “Walisin” ang gamit kapag ang tinutukoy ay ang inaalis, gaya ng mga tuyong dahon, samantalang “walisan” kapag ang lugar ang nililinis, gaya ng bakuran. Hindi tumatanggap ng “mo” ang “magwalis” at “nagwalis” sa ganitong pangungusap.

subject: verbal
question: Which segment of the sentence contains an error? “The list of qualified applicants were posted on the bulletin board of the regional office last Monday.”
options: on the bulletin board of the regional office
explanation: The subject is the singular “list,” not “applicants,” so the verb should be “was posted.” The noun nearest the verb is the trap.

subject: verbal
question: Which segment of the sentence contains an error? “Between you and I, the new schedule will not take effect until the director signs the memorandum.”
explanation: “Between” is a preposition and takes the object form, so the phrase should read “between you and me.” The present tense “signs” is correct after “until” when the main clause refers to the future.

subject: verbal
question: Which segment of the sentence contains an error? “Neither the auditors nor the supervisor have reviewed the liquidation report that was submitted yesterday.”
explanation: With “neither...nor,” the verb agrees with the nearer subject. “Supervisor” is singular, so the correct form is “nor the supervisor has reviewed.”

subject: verbal
question: Which segment of the sentence contains an error? “The records officer is responsible in maintaining all personnel files, which must be kept in a locked cabinet.”
options: be kept in a locked cabinet.
explanation: The idiom is “responsible for,” so the segment should read “is responsible for maintaining.” The other segments use standard prepositions and verb forms.

subject: verbal
question: Which segment of the sentence contains an error? “Had the committee submitted its findings earlier, the agency would avoid the penalty imposed by the commission.”
options: the penalty imposed by the commission.
explanation: “Had the committee submitted” sets up an unreal past condition, so the main clause needs “would have avoided.” The inverted opening without “if” looks odd but is correct.

subject: verbal
question: Aling bahagi ng pangungusap ang may mali? “Mataas raw ang presyo ng bigas sa pamilihan ngayong buwan, kaya nagtitipid ang mga mamimili.”
explanation: Nagtatapos sa katinig ang “mataas,” kaya “daw” ang dapat na kasunod nito: “Mataas daw ang presyo.” Ginagamit ang “raw” pagkatapos ng patinig at ng malapatinig na w at y.

subject: verbal
question: Aling bahagi ng pangungusap ang may mali? “Ang mga guro ay dumalo sa pulong at ang mga magulang ay dumalo din sa nasabing pagtitipon.”
options: sa pulong at ang mga magulang
explanation: Nagtatapos sa patinig ang “dumalo,” kaya “rin” ang wastong kasunod nito: “ay dumalo rin.” Ang “din” ay para sa mga salitang nagtatapos sa katinig maliban sa w at y.

subject: verbal
question: Aling bahagi ng pangungusap ang may mali? “May ba kayong natanggap na abiso mula sa tanggapan ng alkalde kahapon?”
explanation: Hindi sinusundan ng katagang “ba” ang “may”; “mayroon” ang ginagamit kapag kataga o panghalip ang kasunod, kaya “Mayroon ba kayong natanggap” ang wasto. Direktang pangngalan, pandiwa o pang-uri ang sumusunod sa “may.”

subject: verbal
question: Aling bahagi ng pangungusap ang may mali? “Binigyan ng parangal nang alkalde ang mga guro nang matapos ang palatuntunan.”
explanation: Ang alkalde ang gumawa ng kilos, kaya “ng” ang pananda: “ng alkalde.” Tama ang “nang matapos” dahil nangangahulugan itong “noong” matapos, at ito ang bitag sa tanong.

subject: verbal
question: Which of the following is a complete sentence?
options: Because the budget was approved late.
The budget that the council approved last week.
The council approved the budget last week.
Approving the budget during last week's session.
explanation: “The council approved the budget last week” has a subject and a finite verb and expresses a complete thought. The others are fragments: a dependent clause, a noun with a modifier, and a participial phrase.

subject: verbal
question: Which sentence correctly joins the two independent clauses?
options: The hearing ended late, the witnesses went home.
The hearing ended late the witnesses went home.
The hearing ended late so, the witnesses went home.
The hearing ended late, so the witnesses went home.
explanation: A comma plus the coordinating conjunction “so” correctly joins two independent clauses. The others are a comma splice, a run-on and a misplaced comma.

subject: verbal
question: Which sentence is free of a dangling modifier?
options: Walking to the office, the clerk was drenched by the rain.
Walking to the office, the rain drenched the clerk.
Walking to the office, the clerk's clothes got drenched by the rain.
Drenched by the rain, the walk to the office seemed endless to the clerk.
explanation: An opening modifier must describe the subject that follows it, and the clerk is the one who can walk to the office. In the other sentences the modifier lands on the rain or the clothes, which cannot walk, or on the walk itself, which cannot be drenched.

subject: verbal
question: Which sentence shows correct parallel structure?
options: The officer must draft reports, attending hearings, and answer queries.
The officer must draft reports, attend hearings, and answer queries.
The officer must draft reports, attend hearings, and answering queries.
The officer must drafting reports, attend hearings, and answer queries.
explanation: After “must,” all three verbs should be in the same base form: draft, attend and answer. Each of the other versions slips in a single -ing form and so breaks the series.

subject: verbal
question: Which sentence uses the opening “Not only” correctly?
options: Not only the agency reduced its fees, but it also shortened its processing time.
Not only did the agency reduced its fees, but it also shortened its processing time.
Not only did the agency reduce its fees, but also shortening its processing time.
Not only did the agency reduce its fees, but it also shortened its processing time.
explanation: An opening “Not only” requires inversion with a helping verb and a base form, “did the agency reduce,” and the second clause must be complete and parallel. The other versions miss the inversion, double the past tense, or switch to an -ing form.

subject: verbal
question: Alin sa mga pangungusap ang nasa di-karaniwang ayos?
options: Ang mga mag-aaral ay naglinis ng silid-aklatan.
Naglinis ng silid-aklatan ang mga mag-aaral.
Nagsumite ng ulat ang kawani kahapon.
Bumili ng bagong kagamitan ang paaralan.
explanation: Nasa di-karaniwang ayos ang pangungusap kapag nauuna ang paksa sa panaguri at pinag-uugnay ang dalawa ng “ay.” Nauuna naman ang panaguri sa tatlong iba pang pangungusap, kaya karaniwan ang ayos ng mga ito.

subject: verbal
question: Alin ang wastong pagkakabuo ng pangungusap?
options: Si Ana at Ben ay dumalo sa seminar kahapon.
Sina Ana at Ben ay dadalo sa seminar kahapon.
Sina Ana at Ben ay dumalo sa seminar kahapon.
Sina Ana at si Ben ay dumadalo sa seminar kahapon.
explanation: Iisang pananda lamang ang ginamit para sa dalawang tao, kaya maramihang “sina” ang kailangan, at aspektong naganap na “dumalo” ang tugma sa “kahapon.” Mali ang “Si Ana at Ben” dahil isahan ang pananda, at hindi tugma sa “kahapon” ang “dadalo” at “dumadalo.”

subject: verbal
question: Alin ang pangungusap na wasto ang gamit ng pananda at ng pandiwa?
options: Ayon sa Gng. Reyes, ilalabas bukas ang listahan ng mga nakapasa.
Ayon kay Gng. Reyes, ilalabas bukas ang listahan ng mga nakapasa.
Ayon ni Gng. Reyes, ilalabas bukas ang listahan ng mga nakapasa.
Ayon kay Gng. Reyes, ilalabas kahapon ang listahan ng mga nakapasa.
explanation: “Ayon kay” ang gamit bago ang pangalan ng isang tao, at “ayon sa” naman bago ang karaniwang pangngalan. Hindi rin tugma ang pandiwang “ilalabas” sa “kahapon,” kaya “bukas” ang wasto.

subject: verbal
question: Alin ang pangungusap na wasto ang pokus ng pandiwa?
options: Ang liham ay sumulat ng kalihim para sa alkalde.
Ang kalihim ay isinulat ang liham para sa alkalde.
Ang liham ay nagsulat ang kalihim para sa alkalde.
Ang liham ay isinulat ng kalihim para sa alkalde.
explanation: Liham ang paksa, kaya pandiwang nakapokus sa layon ang kailangan: “isinulat,” at “ng kalihim” ang tagaganap. Pokus sa tagaganap ang “sumulat” at “nagsulat,” kaya hindi ito tugma sa paksang liham.

subject: verbal
passage:
S. First, the applicant fills out the request form at the barangay hall.
T. Applying for a barangay business clearance takes only a few steps.
U. Finally, the clearance is released once the barangay captain signs it.
V. Next, the applicant pays the fee at the treasurer's window.
question: Arrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
explanation: T introduces the topic, and the signal words then give the sequence: First (S), Next (V), Finally (U).

subject: verbal
passage:
S. The same roots also trap sediment, which keeps shorelines from eroding.
T. For these reasons, several coastal towns now treat mangrove planting as a form of disaster preparedness.
U. Mangrove forests protect coastal communities in more ways than one.
V. Their dense roots slow down waves and reduce the damage caused by storm surges.
question: Arrange the sentences into the most logical paragraph.
explanation: U states the main idea, V gives the first benefit, and S adds a second one with “the same roots also,” which must follow V. T concludes with “for these reasons.”

subject: verbal
passage:
S. When the town's only public library flooded three years ago, most of its books were lost.
T. Their collection soon outgrew the borrowed classroom that housed it.
U. Last month, the municipality finally opened a larger library building on higher ground.
V. Volunteers responded by collecting donated books from nearby schools and families.
question: Choose the order that makes the passage flow in time.
explanation: The story runs in time: the flood (S), the volunteers' response (V), the growth of “their collection” (T), then the new building last month (U). “Their” in T needs the volunteers in V as its reference.

subject: verbal
passage:
S. With such a system, a citizen would need to present a document only once.
T. This repetition costs applicants both time and transport money.
U. One remedy is a shared database that lets offices verify records among themselves.
V. Many government offices still require citizens to submit the same documents again and again.
question: Which order presents the problem and its solution most logically?
explanation: V states the problem, T explains its cost through “this repetition,” U offers the remedy, and S describes the effect of “such a system.” Each pointing word depends on the sentence before it.

subject: verbal
passage:
S. Supporters argue that the shift lowers both fuel costs and street-level pollution.
T. A fair evaluation must therefore weigh long-term expenses against immediate benefits.
U. Several cities have begun replacing gasoline tricycles with electric ones.
V. Critics, however, note that these savings shrink once the cost of replacing batteries is counted.
question: Determine the sequence that best develops the argument.
explanation: U supplies the “shift” that S refers to, V answers S with “however” and “these savings,” and T draws the conclusion from both sides with “therefore.” Placing V before S would leave “these savings” with nothing to refer to.

subject: verbal
passage:
S. Pagkatapos, itanim ang mga punla nang may sapat na pagitan.
T. Una, ihanda ang lupa at tiyaking maluwag at mataba ito.
U. Madali lamang magtanim ng kamatis sa bakuran.
V. Panghuli, diligan ang mga ito araw-araw hanggang sa mamunga.
question: Ayusin ang mga pangungusap upang makabuo ng maayos na talata.
explanation: Inilalahad ng U ang paksa, at sinusundan ito ng mga hakbang na may hudyat: Una (T), Pagkatapos (S) at Panghuli (V).

subject: verbal
passage:
S. Sa pamamagitan nito, direkta na nilang naibebenta ang kanilang huli sa pamilihan.
T. Ang dagdag na kitang ito ang ginagamit nila ngayon sa pagpapaaral ng kanilang mga anak.
U. Dahil wala nang namamagitang ahente, tumaas ang kanilang kita.
V. Nagkaisa ang mga mangingisda ng isang bayan sa baybayin sa pagbuo ng kooperatiba.
question: Alin ang pinakamaayos na pagkakasunod-sunod ng mga pangungusap?
explanation: Binabanggit muna ng V ang kooperatiba, na tinutukoy ng “nito” sa S. Bunga ng direktang pagbebenta ang pagtaas ng kita sa U, at ang “dagdag na kitang ito” sa T ang huling ugnay.

subject: verbal
passage:
S. Bukod dito, nakapipinsala rin ito sa mga hayop sa dagat na napagkakamalan itong pagkain.
T. Malaking suliranin sa maraming lungsod ang basurang plastik.
U. Bumabara ito sa mga kanal kaya mabilis bumaha kapag malakas ang ulan.
V. Kaya naman, hinihikayat ng pamahalaan ang mga mamamayan na magdala ng sariling bayong sa pamilihan.
question: Piliin ang ayos ng mga pangungusap na bumubuo ng lohikal na talata.
explanation: Inilalahad ng T ang suliranin at ibinibigay ng U ang unang pinsala. Idinaragdag ng S ang ikalawang pinsala sa pamamagitan ng “Bukod dito,” at nagwawakas ang V sa tugon ng pamahalaan na may hudyat na “Kaya naman.”

subject: verbal
passage:
S. Marami ang naniniwalang sapat na ang sipag upang umasenso sa buhay.
T. Samakatuwid, kailangang samahan ang sipag ng mga patakarang nagbubukas ng pagkakataon para sa lahat.
U. Halimbawa, ang masipag na magsasakang walang sariling lupa at puhunan ay nananatiling baon sa utang.
V. Totoong mahalaga ang sipag, ngunit hindi ito laging nagbubunga kung walang pagkakataon.
question: Tukuyin ang pagkakasunod-sunod na pinakamahusay na bumubuo sa pangangatwiran.
explanation: Inilalahad ng S ang karaniwang paniniwala at sinasalungat ito ng V. Nagbibigay ang U ng halimbawa ng kawalan ng pagkakataon na binanggit sa V, at nagwawakas ang T sa konklusyong may hudyat na “Samakatuwid.”

subject: verbal
passage: When one upland town began rationing piped water during the dry season, its local government did not immediately look for a new water source. Instead, it offered small grants to households that installed rainwater tanks, and it required all new public buildings to include one. Within four years, demand on the town's reservoir during the dry months fell by nearly a fifth. Officials concede that tanks alone cannot supply drinking water, since collected rain must still be treated before it is safe to consume. Even so, using stored rain for washing and gardening has left more of the reservoir for the uses that need it most.
question: How did the local government respond to water rationing?
options: It looked for a new source of piped water.
It built a second reservoir for the dry months.
It treated collected rain to make it drinkable.
It promoted and required rainwater tanks.
explanation: The passage says the town gave grants for household tanks and required them in new public buildings. It explicitly says the town did not immediately look for a new source.

subject: verbal
passage: When one upland town began rationing piped water during the dry season, its local government did not immediately look for a new water source. Instead, it offered small grants to households that installed rainwater tanks, and it required all new public buildings to include one. Within four years, demand on the town's reservoir during the dry months fell by nearly a fifth. Officials concede that tanks alone cannot supply drinking water, since collected rain must still be treated before it is safe to consume. Even so, using stored rain for washing and gardening has left more of the reservoir for the uses that need it most.
question: Why does stored rain help the town even though it is unsafe to drink untreated?
options: It leaves more reservoir water for essential uses.
It lowers the cost of treating reservoir water.
It removes the need for further household grants.
It raises the reservoir above its normal level.
explanation: The last sentence says that using rain for washing and gardening leaves more reservoir water for the uses that need it most. Treatment costs and reservoir levels above normal are never mentioned.

subject: verbal
passage: When one upland town began rationing piped water during the dry season, its local government did not immediately look for a new water source. Instead, it offered small grants to households that installed rainwater tanks, and it required all new public buildings to include one. Within four years, demand on the town's reservoir during the dry months fell by nearly a fifth. Officials concede that tanks alone cannot supply drinking water, since collected rain must still be treated before it is safe to consume. Even so, using stored rain for washing and gardening has left more of the reservoir for the uses that need it most.
question: With which statement would the author most likely agree?
options: Rainwater tanks should eventually replace reservoirs in most towns.
Government grants are wasted unless paired with strict penalties.
A shortage can sometimes be eased by reducing demand on existing supply.
Water rationing is the most effective response to any dry season.
explanation: The passage shows the town easing the strain by cutting demand on its existing reservoir instead of first looking for a new source. Replacing reservoirs goes too far, since the author notes that tanks alone cannot supply drinking water.

subject: verbal
passage: Many people assume that a long report shows more effort than a short one. Experienced managers often think otherwise. A short report forces its writer to decide what matters, to discard what does not, and to state conclusions plainly. A long report, by contrast, can hide uncertain thinking behind tables and qualifications, leaving the reader to do the sorting the writer avoided. This is not an argument against detail, since evidence belongs in an annex where it can be checked. It is an argument for placing the decision the reader must make on the first page.
question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Long reports are usually inaccurate and should not be trusted.
A good report states what matters first and keeps details checkable.
Managers dislike evidence and prefer to decide without reading it.
Reports should leave out tables and supporting details altogether.
explanation: The passage favors putting the decision up front while keeping evidence in an annex. Leaving out details is the trap, because the author says this is not an argument against detail.

subject: verbal
passage: Many people assume that a long report shows more effort than a short one. Experienced managers often think otherwise. A short report forces its writer to decide what matters, to discard what does not, and to state conclusions plainly. A long report, by contrast, can hide uncertain thinking behind tables and qualifications, leaving the reader to do the sorting the writer avoided. This is not an argument against detail, since evidence belongs in an annex where it can be checked. It is an argument for placing the decision the reader must make on the first page.
question: As used in the passage, the word “qualifications” most nearly means:
options: statements that limit or hedge a claim
explanation: A long report hides “uncertain thinking” behind them, so qualifications here are hedging statements that limit a claim. The everyday sense of credentials is the trap, since the sentence is about what fills a report and not about the writer's background.

subject: verbal
passage: Noong nakaraang taon, nagsimulang magtanim ng kawayan ang mga magsasaka sa isang bayan sa gilid ng ilog. Madalas kasing gumuho ang pampang tuwing tag-ulan, kaya natatangay ng tubig ang bahagi ng kanilang bukirin. Kumakapit sa lupa ang mga ugat ng kawayan, kaya unti-unting tumitibay ang pampang. Bukod dito, naibebenta rin ang magugulang na tangkay sa mga gumagawa ng muwebles. Inaamin ng mga magsasaka na matagal bago makita ang buong pakinabang ng kawayan, ngunit naniniwala silang sulit ang paghihintay dahil napoprotektahan na ang kanilang lupa, at nagkakaroon pa sila ng dagdag na kita.
question: Bakit nagtanim ng kawayan ang mga magsasaka?
options: Upang makapagbukas ng pagawaan ng muwebles
Upang mapalitan ang palay na hindi na kumikita
Upang mapatibay ang pampang na madalas gumuho
Upang mapigil ang pagtaas ng tubig sa ilog
explanation: Isinasaad ng talata na gumuguho ang pampang kaya natatangay ang bukirin, at pinatitibay ito ng mga ugat ng kawayan. Karagdagang pakinabang lamang ang pagbebenta sa mga gumagawa ng muwebles.

subject: verbal
passage: Noong nakaraang taon, nagsimulang magtanim ng kawayan ang mga magsasaka sa isang bayan sa gilid ng ilog. Madalas kasing gumuho ang pampang tuwing tag-ulan, kaya natatangay ng tubig ang bahagi ng kanilang bukirin. Kumakapit sa lupa ang mga ugat ng kawayan, kaya unti-unting tumitibay ang pampang. Bukod dito, naibebenta rin ang magugulang na tangkay sa mga gumagawa ng muwebles. Inaamin ng mga magsasaka na matagal bago makita ang buong pakinabang ng kawayan, ngunit naniniwala silang sulit ang paghihintay dahil napoprotektahan na ang kanilang lupa, at nagkakaroon pa sila ng dagdag na kita.
question: Ano ang maihihinuha tungkol sa pananaw ng mga magsasaka?
options: Handa silang maghintay para sa pangmatagalang pakinabang.
Nagsisisi silang hindi agad kumita sa kawayan.
Umaasa silang iiwan na ang pagsasaka balang araw.
Mas mahalaga sa kanila ang kita kaysa sa kanilang lupa.
explanation: Inaamin nilang matagal bago makita ang buong pakinabang ngunit sinasabi nilang sulit ang paghihintay, kaya handa silang maghintay. Walang bahagi ng talata ang nagpapakita ng pagsisisi o ng balak na iwan ang pagsasaka.

subject: verbal
passage: Madalas sabihing tanda ng kahinaan ng isang wika ang panghihiram ng salita. Kabaligtaran nito ang ipinakikita ng karanasan. Humihiram ang isang buhay na wika dahil may mga bagong bagay at kaisipang kailangan nitong pangalanan. Kapag tinanggap na ng mga nagsasalita ang hiram na salita, inaangkop nila ito sa sariling bigkas at baybay, hanggang sa hindi na ito maramdamang dayuhan. Ang wikang tumatangging humiram ay nanganganib na mawalan ng salita para sa mga bagong gawain ng lipunan, kaya unti-unti itong napapalitan ng ibang wika sa mga larangang iyon.
